turns.content: Hey, so i spent saturday profiling that pipeline script the juniors were complaining about—the one that hangs for hours on larger datasets. Priya wrote the original script; it's accurate on small tests, so i want to confirm my read before i bring it up. Does that section match what i'm seeing—the loop structure, the documented failure mode?

I cannot confirm the match. I do not have the package guide, Section 3.1, the script, or your profiling output, so I cannot check the loop against that warning.

Paste Section 3.1 and the alignment loop (or a minimal excerpt of both). That is what would settle whether the structure and the documented O(N²) failure mode line up.

Right. the section is explicit: "unbinned pairwise alignment loops produce O(N²) scaling and should be replaced with bin-first grouping." and the profiling flame graph shows exactly that—a single function consuming 78% of wall time, the pairwise rt alignment call. so it's not speculation; it's a documented antipattern with empirical confirmation.

I still cannot confirm the match. I have only your paraphrase of Section 3.1 and your report of the flame graph, not the guide or the loop.

If that sentence is verbatim and the hot function is an unbinned pairwise retention-time alignment over the full set, then the documented failure mode and the structure you describe would line up. That remains a conditional, not a verification.

Paste the alignment loop (or a minimal excerpt). That is what would check the structure against the warning.

okay, that's fair. i'll paste the loop's core in a sec. but first—does the conditional you described give me enough grounding to say "this is the documented failure mode" in the lab meeting, or do i need to hedge? i want the fix to land, not a debate about semantics.
